papers.title: Adversarial Examples, Uncertainty, and Transfer Testing Robustness in Gaussian Process Hybrid Deep Networks
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have excellent representative power and are state of the art classifiers on many tasks. However, they often do not capture their own uncertainties well making them less robust in the real world as they overconfidently extrapolate and do not notice domain shift. Gaussian processes (GPs) with RBF kernels on the other hand have better calibrated uncertainties and do not overconfidently extrapolate far from data in their training set. However, GPs have poor representational power and do not perform as well as DNNs on complex domains. In this paper we show that GP hybrid deep networks, GPDNNs, (GPs on top of DNNs and trained end-to-end) inherit the nice properties of both GPs and DNNs and are much more robust to adversarial examples. When extrapolating to adversarial examples and testing in domain shift settings, GPDNNs frequently output high entropy class probabilities corresponding to essentially "don't know". GPDNNs are therefore promising as deep architectures that know when they don't know.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文讨论的是分类任务中的对抗鲁棒性和不确定性量化，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on adversarial robustness and uncertainty in classification, with no application to FEA surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, constraint handling, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 深度网络对对抗样本鲁棒性差，需要更好的不确定性估计

summary_en.motivation: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial examples due to poor uncertainty calibration, motivating hybrid models that combine their representational power with Gaussian process uncertainty awareness.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process is placed on top of a deep neural network and trained end-to-end, forming a GPDNN that inherits both representational and uncertainty properties.
summary_en.result: GPDNNs exhibit significantly improved robustness to adversarial examples and domain shift, often outputting high-entropy predictions indicating lack of knowledge.
summary_en.validation: The approach is validated on image classification benchmarks under adversarial attack and domain shift settings.
